title: Multifidelity Shadow Scheduler and Data Contract
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines the Multifidelity Shadow Scheduler (MSS) and the accompanying Data Contract used to reliably run shadow evaluations across heterogeneous fidelity levels (live shadow, synthetic micro‑probes, and replayed traffic). The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable orchestration pattern that balances cost, signal quality, and safety for model promotion decisions.

Scope
- Applies to all shadow evaluation runs for inference-serving model variants (hosted, dedicated, private) that feed into promotion gates, regression triage, and quantization verification.
- Describes scheduler behavior, fidelity tiers, data and telemetry contract, acceptance quorum, and runbook for promoting a shadowed candidate.

Motivation
As we increase the cadence of model updates and deploy quantized variants, teams need deterministic, cross‑region shadowing that:
- Produces comparable signal across fidelity types,
- Avoids overloading production paths, and
- Provides a clear data contract so evaluators and SREs can reason about drift and regressions.

Definitions
- Fidelity levels: 'live' (mirror small percentage of live traffic), 'hybrid' (mixed live+synthetic), 'synthetic' (replayer or probe-driven), 'replay' (historical traffic playback).
- Quorum: minimum aggregate of evaluator signals (numeric metrics and human review votes) required before a promotion decision.
- Shadow run: an execution of a model variant in non‑serving mode where outputs are collected for evaluation only.

Design overview
- Scheduler is a central orchestration service (mss-service) that provisions shadow runs to runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private connectors).
- Each run is assigned a fidelity class and a telemetry profile.
- Data Contract guarantees schema, sampling, and retention for evaluation artifacts.
- Promotion flow uses a quorum protocol: numeric gates (SLO deltas, regression thresholds) + at least one manual annotator signoff for high-risk slices.

Key guarantees provided by MSS
- Isolation: shadow traffic must never affect production latency budgets or KV cache integrity.
- Representativeness: live and hybrid runs are weighted to preserve distributional fidelity.
- Reproducibility: replay seeds and probe versions are recorded for exact replays.
- Cost control: synthetic probes have rate limits and backpressure to control GPU spend.

Scheduler algorithm (high level)
1. Accept run request with parameters: model_id, variant_tag, fidelity, slice_spec, duration, tracer_id.
2. Validate data contract: ensure required probes/provenance fields are present. Reject if missing.
3. Allocate capacity using a smoothing window algorithm: prefer idle capacity in same region; fall back to dedicated burst pool.
4. Throttle based on SLO headroom: if p99 latency budget usage > 80% for production pool, route shadow to dedicated or synthetic only.
5. Start run and attach telemetry sampling: full traces for 1% sessions; aggregated metrics for all.
6. Monitor health and auto‑evict after configurable failure thresholds.

Data Contract (required fields)
Every shadow artifact uploaded to the evaluation store must include the following top‑level fields (flat JSON record per request):
| field_name | type | description | required | example |
|------------|------|-------------|----------|---------|
| request_id | string | UUID v4 for the request | yes | req_4f11a2 |
| model_id | string | canonical model slug | yes | gpt-redwood-7b |
| variant_tag | string | serving tag or quant profile | yes | q4_1 |
| fidelity | string | 'live'|'hybrid'|'synthetic'|'replay' | yes | hybrid |
| slice_id | string | logical slice label | yes | payments-card-errors |
| timestamp_utc | string | ISO8601 | yes | 2026-02-18T15:22:03Z |
| input_tokens | int | tokenized input length | yes | 42 |
| output_tokens | int | tokens produced | yes | 128 |
| model_logits_checksum | string | fnv64 hex or 'n/a' for opaque outputs | no | a3f4... |
| provenance | string | 'live-proxy'|'replayer'|'probe-run' | yes | probe-run |
| seed | string | replay/probe seed identifier | conditional | seed_2026_0218 |
| eval_tags | list[string] | tag set for this sample | no | ["anchor","high-confidence"] |

Contract rules
- Records missing required fields are dropped and reported.
- Provenance must be one of the preapproved values listed in the 'provenance registry'.
- For 'live' fidelity, request_id must be correlated with production trace_id for postmortem tracing, but payloads must not be forwarded to downstream systems.

Telemetry and metrics
Minimum metrics emitted by MSS (per run):
- run_id, model_id, variant_tag, fidelity, start_ts, end_ts, total_requests, acceptance_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_count, eviction_reason
- Artifact quality metrics: embedding_stability_score, semantic_similarity_zscore, topk_coverage_delta (for retrieval tasks)
- Cost accounting: gpu_seconds, storage_bytes, network_bytes

Metric SLAs and alerting
- MSS must emit run-level heartbeat every 30s. Missing heartbeat for 2 intervals -> P0 oncall page.
- If synthetic probe failure rate > 5% over 5m -> auto‑scale probe pool down and notify owner.
- If live-shadow p99 latency delta vs prod > 2x baseline for 3 minutes -> auto‑evict runs from production pool.

Quorum and promotion policy
Promotion requires the following:
- Numeric gates: no slice reports > 3% regression in critical task F1 or > 2x latency delta at p95 on production slices.
- Stability gates: embedding stability score >= 0.92 across sampled anchor set.
- Quorum: at least 3 independent automated evaluators pass (unit tests, slice tests, adversarial probes) AND either (a) a human annotator approves critical slices, or (b) an audit of sandboxed inference for 1k samples with no high-severity safety hits.

Promotion flow (operational steps)
1. MSS aggregates run outputs into a promotion report and posts to /eval-reports/{model_id}/{variant_tag}/{run_id}.
2. Auto-evaluator stage runs and emits pass/fail flags.
3. If numeric gates pass and quorum met, the system will mark candidate as 'eligible_for_canary' but will not automatically promote without scheduled canary window.
4. SRE schedules a short canary (0.5% traffic) for 24h with increased monitoring.
5. If canary passes, product owner can approve a staged rollout.

Runbook: quick triage for shadow regressions
1. Identify offending slices from promotion report.
2. Check provenance and fidelity: confirm whether the failure was observed in live/hybrid vs synthetic only.
3. If failure exists only in synthetic runs, reproduce with replay and increased sample size.
4. If failure exists in live-shadow and p99 latency has regressed, evict run and open incident with tag 'shadow-latency'.
5. Use replay with recorded seeds to bisect change set (link to bisect playbook).

APIs & examples
- Start a run (POST /mss/v1/runs): payload must obey data contract header and include 'expected_metrics' list. Example YAML payload:

request: |\n  model_id: redwood-7b\n  variant_tag: q8_0\n  fidelity: hybrid\n  slice_spec:\n    - slice_id: billing-checkout\n      percentage: 0.5\n  duration_minutes: 90\n  tracer_id: mss-20260112-01\n
- Query run status: GET /mss/v1/runs/{run_id}/status -> returns run metadata and last_telemetry_ts.
- Fetch promotion report: GET /eval-reports/{model_id}/{variant_tag}/{run_id} -> JSON stream adhering to data contract.

Configuration reference (table)
| config_key | description | default | ownership |
|------------|-------------|---------|-----------|
| mss.max_live_shadow_pct | Max percent of live requests that can be shadowed per service | 0.5 | platform-sre |
| mss.synthetic_probe_rate | Background probe executions per second per model | 0.1 | eval-platform |
| mss.replay_backoff_seconds | Backoff before replay retries | 60 | eval-platform |
| mss.quorum_min_auto_pass | Minimum number of automated evaluators required | 3 | applied-ml |

Safety and privacy notes
- Live payloads must be scrubbed and PII redacted before storage unless the owning customer has an approved exception.
- Synthetic probes should avoid generating high-risk PII values in prompts.
- Access to promotion reports must be RBAC gated. See security docs for retention windows.

Ownership and SLA
- Owner: applied-ml/inference-evals team (primary: Aisha Raman).
- Platform SLA: MSS control plane 99.9% monthly uptime. Telemetry export latency < 30s for 95% of metrics.

Appendix: example minimal promo report JSON line (flat record)
{ request_id: req_8a9b, model_id: redwood-7b, variant_tag: q8_0, fidelity: hybrid, slice_id: billing-checkout, timestamp_utc: 2026-02-18T15:22:03Z, acceptance_rate: 0.87, p95_latency_ms: 210, embedding_stability_score: 0.96 }

Related work and next steps
- Integrate MSS with the global probe registry to enable auto-rewriting of probes for locale-specific slices.
- Add a policy engine to express conditional fallback rules (e.g., route to quantized-only pool during budget hours).
- Pilot a quorumless fast-path for low-risk performance-only patches.
